input.quote: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Commencing on the later of (i) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Binimetinib Product in the Ono Territory, or (ii) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Encorafenib Product in the Ono Territory, Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement, for any reasons by giving [ * ] advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination.
input.rationale: The term under Section 13.1 runs Product-by-Product and country-by-country until expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term, i.e. many years, yet our at-will exit under Section 13.2 only becomes available on the later of two redacted periods measured from First Commercial Sale of both the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products, and the notice period is redacted. Through the entire development and pre-launch phase we therefore have no convenience right at all, which is the walk-away case of "no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term". The redline removes the First Commercial Sale gate, makes convenience termination operative for Ono as Customer, sets notice at 30 days' written notice and adds the pro-rata refund of prepaid fees required by the preferred position. The Vendor-side element is already met: Array has no convenience right, its routes being cause-based (Section 13.3 material breach, 13.4 bankruptcy, 8.2 exclusivity breach).

ops.newText: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Ono as Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience, for any reasons by giving 30 days' advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination.

ops.text: Upon such termination by Ono under this Section 13.2, Array shall pay Ono a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the First Commercial Sale time-gate so Ono as Customer may terminate for convenience throughout the term, fixed the redacted notice period at 30 days' written notice, and added a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
proposal.summary: Ungate Ono's Section 13.2 convenience termination, set 30 days' notice, and add a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees

mappings.element: No more than 30 days' written notice.
No Vendor termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
mappings.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement in its entirety in the event the other Party shall have materially breached or defaulted in the performance of any of its material obligations hereunder
